- Recoverable periods in Ask (ASK-PERIOD-CONTROL): its approval on master carries over, and it is finished: every part was done before the move. Outcome: A statement question that names no period now asks which period to use instead of refusing, and every settled answer carries a control that moves it to another period without retyping the question. Measured before: 'Show the MIS statement Actual by statement leaf' returned a red refusal 4/4. Measured after: it returns the prompt and the loaded periods, and clicking one returns 81 verified rows with zero selector calls - the chosen period reaches the warehouse as data, never as words re-guessed by the model. Four failure causes that shared one dead-end message now resolve in a fixed order, each saying what is actually wrong: an unresolvable scope triple points at an administrator, a missing mapping and an empty period list keep their own messages, and only a missing period clarifies. An answer that covers no single period says so - 'All loaded data within your access scope and any filters applied by this question' - rather than defaulting a control to a period it never used.
- Reopening a saved report returns to its answer (ASK-REOPEN-SAVED-REPORT): its approval on master carries over, and it is finished: every part was done before the move. Outcome: Opening a saved report or pinned report now returns you to its existing answer instead of stacking a duplicate copy of it. The Ask panel opens immediately on the click rather than after the answer arrives, the target turn is scrolled into view and shows 'Opening this report...' while it runs, and the answer it re-runs is re-asked in your own original wording rather than the pin's measure-name label - so the audit record carries the question someone actually asked. Which turn a report belongs to is decided by strict structural comparison of the resolved selection, not the displayed title, so two pins that both read 'Actual - Budget' but cover different dimensions or periods stay separate answers. A reopen refused because access was withdrawn clears the stale numbers from the screen and says why, while the period control's shipped behaviour of keeping the previous answer is untouched - the caller now states which it wants.
- Assistant + exploration (ASSISTANT): its approval on master carries over, and it is finished: every part was done before the move. Outcome: Srihari can now ask the 3F Financial MIS questions in plain English and get answers he can check. The assistant is registered and governed: every question runs through the same authorization, semantic layer and SQL guard as the reports, so an answer is either the governed numbers with a verified badge and its provenance - the readback, the measures, the scope and the data-as-of behind a disclosure - or an honest refusal that says why. It declines what it must not answer: a causal 'why is labour high' is refused rather than guessed at, a question outside the registered catalog returns not-supported rather than a plausible number, and a greeting is answered deterministically without ever reaching the model. Answers are asked and read in two places, the panel docked beside the MIS report and a standalone Ask page, and 'view in report' opens the statement the answer came from, or says plainly why it cannot. He can save a question and pin it to his dashboard, then reopen either from Explore or the dashboard - and reopening RE-RUNS the saved selection against current data rather than replaying a stored answer, because nothing at rest holds one: the vendored snapshot machinery was deleted outright. Every reopen re-authorizes as the current user against the current semantic layer, so a selection he may no longer run comes back as a refusal that says so rather than a stale figure or a silently missing row, and it stays visible and deletable. The model runs on Bedrock in ap-south-1, and the boundary is enforced by test on the provider's own arguments: his question, the prior turns and the governed vocabulary may leave the app; amounts, measure values, transaction lines and result rows never do.
- Actuals drill-down to transactions (DRILL-DOWN): its approval on master carries over, and it is finished: every part was done before the move. Outcome: Finance can now click any Actual on the Financial MIS and see how it was built. Clicking a group - or the Grand Total - opens a flattened list of every descendant leaf beneath it, footing to the clicked figure in exact paise; clicking a leaf, including the unmapped-GL line, opens the SAP transaction lines behind it in seven columns with a footer that matches the number on the statement. The drill is pinned to the exact actuals and budget batches the displayed statement was built from, so a re-upload can never silently change the answer under the reader's finger: a replaced batch is read and named, and a pin that no longer covers the range is refused with instructions to generate the statement again. Every drill writes a typed audit record before a single row is read and fails closed if that write fails, and refused attempts are audited too - this is the system's only raw-row read path, the documented exception to the aggregate-only rules, so it is the one place where who read which transactions is recoverable. Proven against the client's July extract: a leaf and the unmapped bucket foot in exact paise, the Grand Total reaches 1,00,50,136.29 Budget and 1,15,12,712.07 Actual, and opening a group issues no network request at all.
- Financial semantic layer + governed joins (GOVERNED-JOINS): its approval on master carries over, and it is finished: every part was done before the move. Outcome: The 3F MIS now has ONE governed financial definition — Actual, Budget and % — that report, drill-down and the assistant all share, computed over a correct Budget-Actual join instead of ad-hoc SQL. Each source is first reduced to one ACTIVE row per (gl_code, month), so Budget no longer fans out across a GL's Actual cost centres; the two are then FULL-OUTER-joined with zero-fill, so a Budget-only or Actual-only GL still appears (valued 0.00) instead of vanishing. The % follows the confirmed nil rule in one place: blank/NA when both sides are zero, 'over-budget' when actual spend exists against no budget, and 'credit / negative actual' when that actual is a credit. Access is fail-closed at the single execution boundary — a governed-financial read action plus the domain and every selected measure and dimension grant — and row scope is applied to BOTH sources, so a user scoped away from DUB sees no DUB Budget rows. Every governed number is now explainable: the same composed query returns which sides fed each row (matched / budget-only / actual-only), the deterministic Budget-Components label set, and the ACTIVE source batch ids as (source, period, batch) tuples, with one-sided rows citing only the batch that actually contributed — so when a reload changes an answer, it is attributable to that batch swap. Correctness is frozen behind a golden-answer fixture asserting exact values for all six cases (matched, Budget-only, Actual-only, duplicate/no-fan-out, reload/active-swap, %-edges), demonstrated against a real warehouse (13/13, with a dead-port control proving the proof genuinely connects). This unblocks the MIS reporting epic: the statement, its drill-down and the assistant can now select governed measures rather than author SQL.
- The on-screen assistant explains a number on the MIS statement (MIS-ASSISTANT-EXPLAINS-A-NUMBER): its approval on master carries over, and it is finished: every part was done before the move. Outcome: Click any Actual figure on the MIS statement, ask the assistant beside it how that number came to be, and get an answer built from the same governed data the figure came from. A leaf line answers with both halves: the roll-up path naming the GL codes and cost centres the mapping master folds into it, and the transactions behind it with a footer that foots in paise to the cell you clicked. A subtotal or grand total answers with the lines that compose it and their values, projected in your browser from the statement already on screen rather than fetched again. The assistant still declines to say WHY a number is high - that inference it cannot make - but it will now show exactly WHAT the number is made of, which is the question people were actually asking. Nothing is taken on trust: the statement response carries a signed context binding its scope, outline, pinned batches, mapping-master version and user, so a question can be proven to be about the statement on screen and not merely about data you happen to be entitled to. Every refusal says which check failed. The transaction read keeps the drill's governed-read protections, auditing the exact predicate before it runs and failing closed. No figure the server read ever reaches the model - the explanation is composed on the server and the model only classifies the question. A statement built on a batch that has since been replaced still answers, and says so. The Ask page is untouched: it neither sends this context nor displays these explanations, and a grounded explanation is cleared the moment you generate a different statement, so an answer can never sit against figures it does not describe. SHIPPED UNEXERCISED: no host held both this code and real data, so the capability closes on hermetic proof under decision 0039, and its first run on the server is also its first proof (D-0055).
- Selection + mapping master (MIS-SELECTION): its approval on master carries over, and it is finished: every part was done before the move. Outcome: mis-selection ships the selection layer end to end. A versioned repo-owned Mapping Master is now the single authority for plant aliases, the MIS format and the (cost centre, GL) to MIS-line mapping, with the nine unresolved DUB triples held in an explicit unmapped-GL bucket rather than inferred or dropped. Selection narrows the governed path rather than forking it - the master's resolved triples filter the Actual side before the (gl_code, month) roll-up - and two governed routes expose it. An authenticated user opens MIS Reports, picks Agriculture / Nursery / DUB and a period, presses Generate, and sees the DUB nursery slice from real SAP data: the resolved scope, the totals, the governed GL rows, and the unmapped-GL bucket as a reviewable list carrying an Actual and a Budget amount per GL with the reason each one is unmapped. That list is the artifact that goes to Srihari to get the authoritative mapping back.
- MIS statement + Excel export (MIS-STATEMENT): its approval on master carries over, and it is finished: every part was done before the move. Outcome: 3F can produce the Financial MIS themselves. Pick Agriculture / Nursery / DUB and a period, and Srihari's own statement appears - his hierarchy at its natural depth, his line numbers and budget components, the month and the year-to-date side by side, every parent footing to a grand total of Rs 1,15,12,712 Actual against Rs 1,00,50,136 Budget for July. Download Excel hands him the same statement as a real spreadsheet whose columns sum, named for the selection it came from. The unmapped-GL line stays visible throughout, so the mapping gap he still owes us is impossible to miss rather than absorbed into a total.
- All plants in the MIS statement (MULTI-PLANT): its approval on master carries over, and it is finished: every part was done before the move. Outcome: Every one of the 31 SAP plants in the July extract is now selectable on the MIS Reports screen and renders its own statement on the nursery format, where before only DUB could be chosen. The Department, Function and Plant selectors depend on each other: picking a plant fills in its department and function, picking a department leaves only its functions and plants, and a choice that no longer fits is cleared. The mapping master is generated by a committed script from the client's SAP mapping sheet plus a plant classification table (version 3, 31 plants, 454 cost-centre/GL triples), so a new sheet is a regeneration, not a hand edit; plants whose labels are inferred are marked 'Provisional labels'. Measured: the 31 rendered statements sum to the company net of ₹11,02,73,718.00 in exact paise, and DUB is unchanged against the frozen shipped baseline in values, tree, provenance and Excel bytes. Budget exists only for DUB in the PoC, so every other plant shows a dash for Budget, Roll-over and % (never a zero, never a percentage against nothing) on screen, in the drill and in the export, with an accessible label saying the budget is not loaded for that plant. A user's plant grants come from the seed list, so a demo user can be scoped to one plant. The assistant is untouched by this story.
- Adapt Pulse into the 3F app base (PLATFORM-BASE): its approval on master carries over, and it is finished: every part was done before the move. Outcome: The 3F platform base is shipped end-to-end (all 10 platform-base tasks merged to master, CI green): a vendored NestJS backend on a separate Postgres warehouse with cookie-based email/OTP auth, a trimmed loopback-hardened API allow-list, app-wide observability (a governed constitution-07 error envelope + structured JSON request/error logging correlated by correlationId), a Next.js App Router frontend shell + two-step email/OTP login faithful to the imported 3F design and _ds tokens, and a repo-wide quality gate across all three workspaces (contract+backend+frontend) with dual-runtime + vendor-integrity checks and CI verify on every push. A user can sign in to the shell; the factory can build, verify, and ship the next epic on a green, guarded foundation.
- Assistant responsiveness and shell truth (POC-RESPONSIVENESS): its approval on master carries over, and it is finished: every part was done before the move. Outcome: A follow-up question used to take 39 seconds, then 57, and looked like the product had hung. It now comes back in one to five seconds, and while it works you can see it working: both Ask surfaces stream the backend's own progress phases - routing, selecting, querying, summarizing - instead of one silent spinner, and an answer that arrives immediately shows no flicker at all. The cause turned out to be a single missing request field: the selector call to Bedrock set no output limit, so on a follow-up the model would emit up to twenty-four thousand tokens of preamble around a hundred-token answer. Capping it ended the runaway without truncating anything. Leaving the assistant now actually stops the work rather than abandoning it, and asking a ninth question in one conversation no longer fails - the client sends only as much history as the server accepts. The shell's top bar stops lying: where it showed a permanently greyed-out 'Freshness unavailable' chip, it now shows when the governed data was last loaded, taken from the oldest active batch across actuals and budget so it never claims the numbers are fresher than the stalest input behind them, and it says plainly which kind of unavailable it is when there is nothing to show. The docked Ask panel fills its column instead of stopping halfway down the page.
- Ingest SAP actuals + budgets (SAP-INGESTION): its approval on master carries over, and it is finished: every part was done before the move. Outcome: sap-ingestion delivers the Financial MIS data foundation: SAP actuals and MIS budgets ingest into a dedicated warehouse (guarded POST /api/ingest/actuals and /budget), each upload replaced idempotently per period with prior-batch retention, and the headline figure is proven to source — July 2026 DUB actuals reconcile to EXACTLY Rs 11,512,712.07 (paise) across both the raw sap_transaction rows and the actual_by_key_month gold view, stable under re-upload. Four tasks shipped: warehouse-schema (#13), actuals-loader (#15), budget-loader (#16), reconciliation-proof (#17). No governed budget-actual join or UI yet (governed-joins / reporting stories).
